docs.title: FlapSim: A Composable MuJoCo Simulation Platform and Reduced-Order Aerodynamic Model Hierarchy for Flapping-Wing Robotics

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text:
Flapping-wing simulation must reconcile high-frequency wingbeat aerodynamics with the slower dynamics relevant to flight control and reinforcement learning. We present FlapSim, a modular open-source MuJoCo simulation platform that combines robot descriptions, wing geometry, and composable aerodynamic models in a deterministic simulation pipeline. Across 48 held-out scenarios spanning frequency, gimbal, wind, frequency-step, gust, and cross-robot flat-plate regimes, we compare five reduced-order configurations operating at 1 ms with a 50 µs quasi-steady blade-element reference. The built-in hover cycle-averaged baseline achieves a 67.51× CPU speedup but only 0.6593 mean wrench fidelity. Combining multirate 21-substep clock synchronization, three-dimensional linear/quadratic inflow and gust coupling, analytical blade-element geometry scaling, and phase-locked 1f–6f harmonics raises mean fidelity to 0.9646 at a 65.19× speedup in a five-block model. A streamlined four-block model without explicit step-transient lag states achieves 0.9662 fidelity at a 67.98× speedup. Controlled ablations show that stroke harmonics are particularly important during frequency transitions, improving held-out frequency-step fidelity by +0.3176. Transfer-function analysis explains this effect: fixed-window cycle averaging retains harmonic contributions when the wingbeat frequency changes, so within-cycle reconstruction also improves the filtered wrench. Once phase alignment and harmonic synthesis are included, explicit transient lag states provide no additional benefit in this benchmark. These results characterize the accuracy–computation tradeoff of the aerodynamic hierarchy and identify timing, inflow, geometry, and harmonic representation as central considerations for reduced-order flapping-wing simulation.

docs.title: Contributions
docs.text:
1. Platform architecture and software characterization. FlapSim's software architecture, robot manifest and CAD/MJCF/URDF import pipeline, first-class wing planform integral engine, phase-ordered plugin execution loop, Gymnasium learning interfaces and identification tooling.
  2. Quantitative characterization of the reduced-order aerodynamic hierarchy. Five 1 ms reduced-order configurations benchmarked against the 50 µs per-step blade-element reference across six operating regimes, with controlled ablations and a transfer-function analysis of why within-cycle harmonics matter.

docs.title: Platform
docs.text:
Architecture and aerodynamic model hierarchy. (a) Robot descriptions and wing geometry are assembled into a MuJoCo simulation with a deterministic sequence of sensing, control, actuation, force evaluation, integration, post-step updates and recording; plugins exchange state through a shared signal bus. (b) The hierarchy connects the 50 µs blade-element reference to alternative 1 ms reduced models; dashed connections denote offline identification. (PDF)

  • Bring your own robot

    URDF, MJCF or a programmatic MjSpec, plus a small robot.yaml that names the wings, their frames, stroke and feathering joints, planform and mass model. Import your robot →

  • Composable aerodynamics

    Quasi-steady blade-element forces at the centre of pressure, rotational lift, added mass, wake capture, ground effect, wind, gusts and body drag, stacked per wing. Aerodynamic models →

  • Everything is a plugin

    Actuators, sensors, controllers, atmosphere and recorders share one step pipeline and a signal bus; third-party plugins register through an entry point. Write a plugin →

  • Identification and learning

    flapsim sweep identifies cycle-averaged models from the per-step reference; SimulationEnv turns any setup into a Gymnasium environment. Learning and studies →

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Held-out benchmark of five 1 ms configurations against the 50 µs blade-element reference, mean wrench fidelity over all 48 scenarios (Table III b of the paper):

Configuration Mean fidelity CPU speedup Training Hover cycle-averaged (built in) 0.6593 67.51× 22.5 s LQ wind-lag 0.8280 68.29× 137.3 s Mean-only (no harmonics) 0.8987 66.25× 137.8 s Five-block harmonic 0.9646 65.19× 160.5 s Four-block harmonic 0.9662 67.98× 165.0 s

Wrench fidelity across the hierarchy. (a) Mean fidelity in each flight regime (n = 8 scenarios per regime). (b) Mean fidelity across all 48 scenarios, from 0.6593 for the hover cycle-averaged baseline to 0.9662 for the four-block harmonic model. Error bars: ±1 sample SD across scenarios. (PDF)

Computational speedup and component ablations. (a) CPU speedup by regime relative to the reference simulator; the dashed line marks the 20× score-saturation threshold. (b) Changes in frequency-step and overall fidelity when removing harmonics, explicit transient states or clock synchronization (frequency-step changes −0.3176, +0.0095 and −0.3243). (PDF)

Force and torque errors by regime. Normalized force error (a) and torque error (b) on logarithmic axes; wind force error falls 50.1× (1.8124 → 0.0362) and flat-plate force error 27.3× (0.6030 → 0.0221). (PDF)

Harmonic reconstruction and moving-average filter leakage. Harmonic synthesis reduces raw force RMSE 6.65× (0.4166 N → 0.0627 N); the frequency-step improvement of +0.3680 is consistent with cancelling the 244.2× increase in fundamental-frequency transmission at the higher wingbeat frequency. (PDF)

Further analyses: force–torque asymmetry and ridge-regression conditioning

Force–torque asymmetry and fidelity dispersion. (a) Mean scenario-wise error ratio with ±1 sample SD (n = 8 per regime). (b) Minimum–maximum ranges and medians of the five-block model's fidelity. (PDF)

Ridge-regression conditioning and sensitivity to the phase model. Subtracting the harmonic predictions before the final stage avoids a 5.13× increase in weight norm; cross-validation compares six phase conventions and harmonic weights. (PDF)

Benchmark numbers are those reported in the paper, evaluated at revision 19fa57f. The repository has since gained fixes to the optional rotational-lift and added-mass models (see the changelog); the quasi-steady reference and its lift regression are unchanged.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/MingshanHe/FlapSim.git && cd FlapSim
pip install -e ".[dev]"
flapsim run SingleThrustFlapper                    # viewer, fixed base, force arrows
flapsim run SingleThrustFlapper --config hover     # floating base, hover PID
flapsim inspect my_robot.urdf                      # bodies and joints for your manifest

from flapsim import Simulation

sim = Simulation("SingleThrustFlapper")
sim.add({"type": "actuator/sinusoidal_stroke", "id": "stroke",
         "joints": ["left_flapping_joint", "right_wing_flapping"],
         "directions": [1, -1], "frequency_hz": 40.0, "amplitude_rad": 1.5})
sim.add({"type": "aero/stack", "models": ["quasi_steady", "rotational_lift"]})
sim.add({"type": "recorder/memory", "signals": ["aero/F_world"], "every": 1e-3})
sim.run(1.0)
print(sim["recorder"]["aero/F_world"][:, 2].mean(), "N mean lift")

More in Getting started, the gallery and the API reference.

docs.title: Aerodynamic models
docs.text:
FlapSim's aerodynamics are additive per-wing models evaluated by one engine (flapsim.aero.AeroEngine). The engine computes each wing's relative-flow kinematics once per step, asks every model for its loads (a force at a point plus a pure moment, all in the wing aero frame), multiplies the sum by the modifiers' factors and writes the wrench to MuJoCo. Plugins expose the engine: aero/quasi_steady is the single-model stack, aero/stack composes models.

- type: aero/stack
  models:
    - quasi_steady
    - rotational_lift
    - {type: added_mass, include_rotational_inertia: true}
    - {type: wake_capture, C_wc: 0.8}
  modifiers:
    - {type: ground_effect, model: exponential, gain: 0.3}

Signals: aero/F_world, aero/lift_total, aero/rho, per wing wings/<name>/F_N (total normal force), alpha, U_i, U_o, F_world, torque_world, cop_world, and per model wings/<name>/<model>/<key>.

docs.title: Models
docs.text: Model Physics Parameters Reference quasi_steady Translational normal force 1/2 rho c C_N(alpha) (U^2 integrals) at the centre of pressure, pitching moment through the chordwise CoP, rotational damping M_rd options (AeroOptions overrides) Whitney & Wood 2010; Dickinson et al. 1999 fits rotational_lift C_rot rho theta_dot integral c^2 |U| dr (flow-speed magnitude, so the force flips between strokes), positive when pitching up into the flow, at the half chord C_rot (default pi (0.75 - x0)), point_fraction Sane & Dickinson 2002 added_mass Explicit force integral (rho pi c^2 / 4) dU_n/dt dr from the prescribed stroke and body accelerations; the added rotational inertia about the feathering hinge is added to the joint armature (implicit, stable for light wings) include_feathering_inertia Sedov; Sane & Dickinson 2002 wake_capture Empirical transient C_wc 1/2 rho S U_rev^2 exp(-t/tau) after each stroke reversal C_wc, tau_chords, point_fraction, min_speed Dickinson et al. 1999 (phenomenon)

docs.title: Modifiers
docs.text: Modifier Factor Parameters ground_effect 1 + gain exp(-h / (length_scale R)) or Cheeseman-Bennett 1 / (1 - (R / 4h)^2) model, gain, length_scale, ground_height, max_factor

docs.title: Related plugins
docs.text:
• atmosphere/standard: density (ISA at altitude_m or rho), steady wind, a gust (one_minus_cos, sine, step) and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck turbulence. Publishes atmosphere/rho and atmosphere/wind_world, which the aero stack and body drag read.
  • force/body_drag: -1/2 rho C_d A |v| v per body axis relative to the wind.
  • aero/cycle_averaged: rigid-body hover model, lift = k f^2 along the gimbal-tilted thrust axis plus control moments and damping. Parameters come from flapsim sweep (flapsim.aero.identify), which runs the fixed-base per-step model as a virtual wind tunnel: frequency sweep for k, gimbal deflections for thrust tilt and moments per radian, imposed body velocities and rates for damping.

docs.title: Writing a model
docs.text:
from flapsim.aero import AeroModel, WingLoads, register_model
import numpy as np


@register_model
class MyModel(AeroModel):
    name = "my_model"

    def compute(self, wing, state, kin, flow, options):
        force_n = ...  # along the wing normal
        point = np.array([0.0, state.side * kin["span_CoP"], -0.5 * wing.mean_chord])
        return WingLoads(
            self.name, np.array([force_n, 0, 0]), point, np.zeros(3), {"k": 1.0}
        )

kin holds the shared kinematics (U_i1, U_i0, U_o1, U_o0, alpha, span_CoP, theta_dot, ...), flow the air density, wind and torso velocity, wing.params the planform (R, c, integrals, hinge geometry). Models shipped in another package register through the same decorator and become available by name in aero/stack configs.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to FlapSim are recorded here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project uses Semantic Versioning.
First release of FlapSim as an open platform. Everything below was built on the open-platform branch on top of the 0.1.0 single-robot simulator.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• English translations of the quasi-steady derivation, the hover simplification and the two engineering notes (docs/derivations, docs/notes); the Chinese originals stay under docs/zh/.
  • Learning: flapsim.envs.SimulationEnv Gymnasium wrapper (observations from signals, actions to commands with smoothing), hover_reward, hover_terminated; flapsim.study.parameter_study (parallel grids); examples/rl/ IMU + TOF hover task with PPO training/evaluation scripts; examples/wing_length_study.py; extras rl, video, hdf5; RL CI job.
  • Components: sensors sensor/imu, sensor/rangefinder (plane or ray), sensor/encoder, sensor/wrench (load cell) with a shared conditioner (sample rate, low-pass, delay, noise, per-episode bias, quantisation); actuators actuator/dc_motor_crank (voltage-driven motor, gearbox and crank loaded by the aero torques) and actuator/servo (rate-limited, lagged PD); controllers controller/schedule and controller/callback; ForceArrows viewer overlay, record_video (GIF, PNG frames, MP4), recorder HDF5 export; flapsim record and flapsim run --overlay; examples hover_pid.py, sensors.py, lift_sweep.py, custom_aero_model.py, render_video.py.
  • Aerodynamics library: AeroEngine evaluating additive per-wing models with shared kinematics; models quasi_steady, rotational_lift, added_mass, wake_capture; modifier ground_effect; aero/stack plugin; atmosphere/standard (ISA density, wind, gusts, turbulence); force/body_drag; aero/cycle_averaged generalized to identified thrust-tilt and moment matrices with parameter files; flapsim sweep identification (frequency, gimbal and damping sweeps). docs/aero_models.md.
  • Plugin system: flapsim.core.Simulation with the phases pre_control, control, actuate, forces, mj_step, post_step, record; a signal bus (wings/left/alpha, cmd/stroke/frequency_hz, ...); plugin base classes; a registry addressed by kind/name with entry-point discovery (flapsim.plugins group); flapsim.sim/1 YAML/JSON simulation configs with per-plugin overrides.
  • Built-in plugins: actuator/sinusoidal_stroke, actuator/pd_position (with joint roles), aero/quasi_steady, aero/cycle_averaged, controller/hover_pid, recorder/memory (npz/csv export).
  • flapsim.testing.check_plugin conformance check for third-party plugins; flapsim plugins and flapsim run <config.yaml> --describe commands; flat_plate_simulation() helper.
  • Example robot ships sim.yaml (fixed base) and hover.yaml (floating base) next to its manifest.
  • Robot manifests (robot.yaml): wings with aero frames, stroke and feathering joints, planforms, mirror relations; model patches for joint dynamics, equalities, mass overrides and collision exclusion; when: free / when: fixed conditional patches.
  • flapsim.robot.load() accepting built-in names, manifests, bare URDF/MJCF files and MjSpec objects; builtin_robots(); RobotModel with Wing objects.
  • flapsim.wings: planform integrals from analytic profiles, chord polylines, planform polygons and STL mesh outlines; runtime Wing state.
  • flapsim.robot.flat_plate_flapper() parametric two-wing robot built in Python (no CAD needed).
  • flapsim inspect and flapsim run command line (python -m flapsim.cli).
  • The quasi-steady adapter now handles any number of wings from the manifest.
  • Per-wing mass_model (spar_plate, thin_plate, explicit) declared in wing coordinates and converted to each body frame, so mirrored wings share one description; hinge geometry (pitch_axis_fraction, leading_edge_offset) in the planform and the aerodynamic moment.
  • Geometry self-checks at load time: warnings when a wing's chord direction or a joint sign looks reversed.
  • docs/derivations/quasi_steady_model.md: frame conventions, equations, hinge geometry, the passive-feathering regime and the model correction.
  • Apache-2.0 license, NOTICE, contributing guide, code of conduct, citation file.
  • Test suite: aerodynamic unit tests, left/right symmetry test, fixed-base lift-sweep regression test, headless smoke tests.
  • GitHub Actions CI (ruff + pytest on Linux, macOS, Windows; Python 3.10-3.13).
  • ROADMAP.md describing the open-platform architecture and phases.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• added_mass: the feathering part of the added mass was an explicit force built from a one-step finite-difference feathering acceleration, which diverged on the 0.06 g wings (force pinned at the 5 N limit). The added rotational inertia is now added to the feathering joint's armature (implicit); only the prescribed stroke and body accelerations stay explicit. New AeroModel.bind(robot) hook.
  • rotational_lift: used the signed flow speed, so the force did not flip between upstroke and downstroke and the passive feathering became asymmetric; it now uses the flow-speed magnitude, evaluated at the c²-weighted span centroid (exact while the flow keeps its sign, continuous through reversal).
  • ForceArrows cleared the scene when used with the offscreen renderer, so rendered videos showed only the arrows; it now appends to renderer scenes and clears only a viewer's private overlay scene.
  • Manifest equality constraints size their data from mujoco.mjNEQDATA, so the example robot loads with MuJoCo releases where that constant is 12 (reported against mujoco 3.17).
  • flat_plate_flapper: a fresh MjSpec interprets angles in degrees, so the builder's joint ranges were 57 times too small; it now declares radians, uses stiff limit solver constants and a spar-plate wing mass model, and produces positive lift with correctly phased passive feathering.
  • Actuators restore their configured targets and commands on reset(), so episodes are deterministic for a given seed.
  • Quasi-steady pitching moment: the earlier implementation multiplied the moment by sign(alpha), which made it independent of the flow direction and moved the centre of pressure to the opposite side of the hinge at each stroke reversal; the MuJoCo adapter compensated with a translational force flip. The moment is now -(x_le + (d_cp - x0) c) F_N with the centre of pressure fixed on the plate, the flip is gone, and the wing frame is defined by span and chord so the plate side is explicit. See docs/derivations/quasi_steady_model.md. Regression values were re-measured.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:

  • SimCore loads any robot that provides extras.joints; PlateController, HoveringController and AveragedHoverAero take joint and body names from configuration instead of hard-coding them.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
flapsim run      [source] [--config NAME] [--base fixed|free] [--headless]
                 [--duration S] [--frequency HZ] [--amplitude RAD]
                 [--overlay forces|none] [--describe]
flapsim inspect  <source> [--base fixed|free] [--json]
flapsim plugins  [--kind KIND]
flapsim sweep    [source] [--frequencies ...] [--reference HZ] [--amplitude RAD]
                 [--gimbal-angle RAD] [--settle S] [--cycles N] [--no-damping]
                 [--output params.yaml]
flapsim record   [source] --output clip.gif|clip.mp4|frames_dir [--duration S]
                 [--fps N] [--width W] [--height H] [--camera NAME] [--slow F]

source is a built-in robot name (SingleThrustFlapper), a robot manifest, a bare URDF/MJCF file, or a flapsim.sim/1 setup file. For a robot, run uses the sim.yaml next to its manifest, or <NAME>.yaml with --config (--base free picks hover.yaml).

sweep runs the fixed-base setup as a virtual wind tunnel and writes a flapsim.cycle_averaged/1 parameter file for aero/cycle_averaged.

python flapsim.py --robot NAME [--fix false] [--headless --duration S] is the pre-platform entry point and still works.

docs.title: Component plugins
docs.text: All components are plugins (see flapsim plugins). They exchange named signals: a sensor publishes imu/gyro, a controller reads it and publishes cmd/stroke/frequency_hz, the stroke actuator consumes the command. Plugins run in insertion order within each phase (pre_control for sensors, control for controllers, actuate for actuators, forces for aero).

docs.title: Actuators
docs.text: Plugin What it does Commands Signals actuator/sinusoidal_stroke Kinematic q = d A sin(2 pi f t) on stroke joints (kinematic writes velocities, position_only does not) frequency_hz, amplitude_rad frequency_hz, amplitude_rad, phase actuator/pd_position Gravity-compensated PD with torque limit, or kinematic hold; joints carry a role label <joint> target <joint> actuator/servo pd_position with a rate-limited, first-order lagged target <joint> desired <joint>, <joint>/desired actuator/dc_motor_crank DC motor (i = (V - k_e w)/R, tau = k_t i), gearbox N, crank q = d A sin(theta_c); loaded by the aero torque about the stroke joints voltage_v speed_rad_s, frequency_hz, current_a, torque_load, power_w, ...

docs.title: Sensors
docs.text:
Every sensor samples at rate_hz through a Conditioner: first-order low-pass tau, pure delay delay_s, Gaussian noise_std, a bias drawn per episode from bias_range, and quantisation resolution.

Plugin Measures Defaults sensor/imu euler (low-passed attitude), gyro (body rates), accel (specific force R^T (a - g)), quat 500 Hz, 20 ms attitude lag, 0.02 deg / 0.002 rad/s / 0.02 m/s^2 noise, 0.01 m/s^2 bias sensor/rangefinder slant range along a body axis to the ground plane or by ray cast, range_rate 500 Hz, 20 ms delay, 5 mm noise, 4 m range sensor/encoder joint position (quantised by counts_per_rev) and velocity continuous sensor/wrench interaction wrench with the parent body (cfrc_int): a load cell under a fixed-base robot averaging average_s

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install flapsim                 # core: MuJoCo, NumPy, PyYAML
pip install "flapsim[rl]"           # + Gymnasium (add stable-baselines3 for PPO)
pip install "flapsim[video,hdf5]"   # + imageio/ffmpeg video, h5py export

From a checkout: pip install -e ".[dev]" then pytest -q.

Python 3.10 or newer; MuJoCo 3.3 or newer is installed automatically. On a headless machine set MUJOCO_GL=osmesa or MUJOCO_GL=egl for rendering.

docs.title: Run the example robot
docs.text:
The package ships a 30 g single-thrust flapper (two passive-feathering wings on a two-axis gimbal) with two setups:

flapsim run SingleThrustFlapper                       # sim.yaml: fixed base, quasi-steady aero
flapsim run SingleThrustFlapper --config hover        # hover.yaml: floating base, hover PID
flapsim run SingleThrustFlapper --headless --duration 2 --frequency 40
flapsim run SingleThrustFlapper --describe            # the assembled plugins and signals

docs.title: Assemble a simulation in Python
docs.text:
from flapsim import Simulation

sim = Simulation("SingleThrustFlapper")  # or a robot.yaml / URDF / MJCF path
sim.add(
    {
        "type": "actuator/sinusoidal_stroke",
        "id": "stroke",
        "joints": ["left_flapping_joint", "right_wing_flapping"],
        "directions": [1, -1],
        "frequency_hz": 40.0,
        "amplitude_rad": 1.5,
    }
)
sim.add("aero/quasi_steady")
sim.add({"type": "sensor/imu", "rate_hz": 500.0})
sim.add(
    {"type": "recorder/memory", "signals": ["aero/F_world", "imu/*"], "every": 1e-3}
)

sim.run(1.0)  # headless
rec = sim["recorder"]
print(rec["aero/F_world"][:, 2].mean())
rec.to_csv("run.csv")

Plugins are addressed by kind/name (flapsim plugins lists them). They communicate through named signals: the aero plugin publishes wings/left/alpha, the IMU publishes imu/gyro, a controller publishes cmd/stroke/frequency_hz and the stroke actuator obeys it.

docs.title: Or write a setup file
docs.text:
# my_sim.yaml
schema: flapsim.sim/1
robot: SingleThrustFlapper          # or a path to robot.yaml / model file
plugins:
  - type: actuator/sinusoidal_stroke
    id: stroke
    joints: [left_flapping_joint, right_wing_flapping]
    directions: [1, -1]
    frequency_hz: 40.0
    amplitude_rad: 1.5
  - type: atmosphere/standard
    wind: [0.5, 0.0, 0.0]
  - type: aero/stack
    models: [quasi_steady, rotational_lift, added_mass]
  - type: recorder/memory
    signals: ["aero/F_world", "wings/*/alpha"]
    every: 1.0e-3
run:
  duration: 2.0

flapsim run my_sim.yaml --headless
flapsim record my_sim.yaml --output clip.gif --duration 0.1 --slow 20

docs.title: Write a plugin
docs.text:
A plugin is a Python class bound to one Simulation. It takes part in the step phases it overrides and talks to other plugins through named signals.

pre_control  sensors read the state and publish readings
control      controllers read signals, publish cmd/<plugin>/<name>
actuate      actuators drive joints (torques or kinematic targets)
forces       force models write xfrc_applied
mj_step
post_step    kinematic actuators re-impose targets (return True if qpos changed)
record       recorders sample the signal bus

docs.title: A minimal force plugin
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from flapsim.plugins import ForcePlugin, register


@register
class ConstantThrust(ForcePlugin):
    name = "constant_thrust"  # addressed as force/constant_thrust
    provides = ("force",)  # signals you promise to publish
    example_config = {"body": "base_link", "newtons": 0.1}

    def __init__(self, *, body, newtons=0.1, id=None):
        super().__init__(id=id, body=body, newtons=newtons)
        self.body_name, self.newtons = body, float(newtons)

    def setup(self):  # resolve MuJoCo ids once
        import mujoco

        self.body_id = mujoco.mj_name2id(
            self.model, mujoco.mjtObj.mjOBJ_BODY, self.body_name
        )
        if self.body_id < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"body {self.body_name!r} not found")

    def forces(self):
        force = np.array([0.0, 0.0, self.command("newtons", self.newtons)])
        self.data.xfrc_applied[self.body_id, :3] += force
        self.publish("force", force)

Use it with sim.add(ConstantThrust(body="base_link")), by name sim.add({"type": "force/constant_thrust", "body": "base_link"}), or from a setup file. self.command("newtons") reads cmd/<id>/newtons, so any controller can drive it.

docs.title: Plugin kinds
docs.text: Plugin, ForcePlugin, AeroPlugin, AtmospherePlugin, ActuatorPlugin, SensorPlugin, ControllerPlugin, RecorderPlugin set the kind. Aero models (additive per-wing loads) are not plugins but AeroModel subclasses registered with flapsim.aero.register_model; see Aerodynamic models.

docs.title: Ship it as a package
docs.text:
Declare an entry point so pip install my-flapsim-plugins makes your plugins available by name:

[project.entry-points."flapsim.plugins"]
my_plugins = "my_package.plugins"      # a module that registers on import,
                                       # a Plugin class, or a callable

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
from flapsim.testing import check_plugin

check_plugin(lambda: ConstantThrust(body="base_link"))

The conformance check attaches the plugin to the example robot, steps, resets, steps again, verifies declared signals and that describe() is JSON-serialisable. Run it in your own test suite.

docs.title: Reinforcement learning and parameter studies
docs.text: Install the extra: pip install "flapsim[rl]" (Gymnasium; add stable-baselines3 for the PPO scripts).

docs.title: SimulationEnv
docs.text:
flapsim.envs.SimulationEnv wraps any simulation as a Gymnasium environment. You list the signals that form the observation and the commands that the action drives; everything else stays in plugins.

from flapsim.envs import SimulationEnv, hover_reward, hover_terminated

env = SimulationEnv(
    make_sim,  # () -> Simulation (sensors included)
    observations=[
        "imu/euler",
        "imu/gyro",
        {"signal": "imu/accel", "scale": 0.1},
        "tof/range",
        "tof/range_rate",
    ],
    actions=[
        {"command": "gimbal/pitch_joint", "low": -0.3, "high": 0.3, "tau": 0.0082},
        {"command": "gimbal/roll_joint", "low": -0.3, "high": 0.3, "tau": 0.0082},
        {"command": "stroke/frequency_hz", "low": 36.0, "high": 44.0, "initial": 40.0},
    ],
    decision_dt=0.01,
    episode_seconds=6.0,
    reward=hover_reward(0.5),
    terminated=hover_terminated(),
    on_reset=randomize,
)
  • Actions live in [-1, 1] and map affinely onto [low, high]; tau adds a first-order lag between the command and the actuator (actuator dynamics or a communication filter).
  • include_previous_action appends the last action to the observation.
  • reward(env, obs, action) may return (value, terms); the terms land in info["reward_terms"]. hover_reward and hover_terminated reproduce the IMU-hover training signal (true-state reward, sensor-only observation).
  • on_reset(env) randomises the initial state or plugin parameters using env.rng.

The environment passes gymnasium.utils.env_checker.check_env.

docs.title: The IMU + TOF hover example
docs.text:
examples/rl/imu_hover_env.py rebuilds the sensor-only hover task on the floating-base cycle-averaged model: 14-dimensional observation (attitude, rates, specific force, range, range rate, previous action), three actions (gimbal pitch, gimbal roll, stroke frequency within +/- 10 % of hover).

python examples/rl/train_ppo.py --timesteps 500000 --n-envs 4 --output models/imu_hover_ppo
python examples/rl/evaluate.py --model models/imu_hover_ppo.zip --episodes 10
python examples/rl/evaluate.py --baseline --episodes 3          # zero-action reference

Trained policies and logs are not committed (models/*.zip, runs/ are ignored).

docs.title: Parameter studies
docs.text: flapsim.study.parameter_study(evaluate, grid, workers=n) evaluates a module-level function over the Cartesian product of parameter lists in parallel processes, captures per-case errors, and returns a StudyResult with rows(), best(metric) and to_csv(). See examples/wing_length_study.py (lift of the flat-plate flapper versus span and frequency) and flapsim sweep for the cycle-averaged identification.

docs.title: FlapSim open-platform plan
docs.text:
Branch: open-platform (cut from master on 2026-10-28, all training code and data removed) Status: Phases 0-7 complete; release 0.2.0 prepared (see section 9)

FlapSim becomes an open-source simulation platform for flapping-wing robots built on MuJoCo. A user brings their own robot description, tells FlapSim which bodies are wings, picks aerodynamic models and other components from a plugin registry, and runs the simulation headless or in the viewer. Everything specific to one robot lives in that robot's description package, not in flapsim/.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. Import any robot. URDF (today), MJCF, a programmatic mujoco.MjSpec, or a parametric builder for users without CAD.
  2. Wings as first-class objects. A robot manifest declares which bodies are wings, their aerodynamic frame, stroke and feathering joints, and planform geometry. FlapSim derives wing kinematics from the MuJoCo state and computes lift, drag and moments.
  3. Aerodynamics as plugins. Quasi-steady blade-element (the current FlapX derived model), cycle-averaged, rotational lift, added mass, wake capture, body drag, ground effect, wind and gusts. Users can stack built-in models or ship their own in a separate pip package.
  4. Other components as plugins. Actuators, sensors, controllers, recorders and viewer overlays use the same plugin API and the same step pipeline.
  5. Reproducible science. Regression tests pin the validated numbers (the fixed-base lift sweep, FlapX parity). Every result a paper cites can be regenerated with one command.
  6. Usable by outsiders. README, tutorials, API docs, CI, PyPI package, contribution guide, permissive license, citation file.

docs.title: Non-goals (for now)
docs.text:
• CFD or vortex-lattice fluid solvers. The plugin interface allows them later.
  • GPU batch simulation (MJX). Measured earlier: per-step cost with the joint equality constraints was far worse than CPU MuJoCo. Keep CPU-first.
  • Hardware-in-the-loop. Firmware lives outside this repo.

docs.title: 2. Baseline audit (what the branch contains today)
docs.text:
Area File(s) State Step loop flapsim/environment/environment.py Already a proto pipeline: supervisors, control pairs, force models, mj_step, post_step. Good seed for plugin phases. URDF import environment.py via MjSpec.from_file Works, but patches robot-specific joints (left_wing_feathering), adds a mirror equality and overrides the floating-base mass to 30 g in code. Scene flapsim/environment/scene.py Generic, reusable. Aero (pure) flapsim/fluid/aero.py Quasi-steady blade-element model, pure functions, SI units, well documented in tutorial/aero.md. Hard-coded to exactly two wings (left/right). Aero (MuJoCo) flapsim/fluid/mujoco_adapter.py Hard-codes body names link2, left_wing, right_wing, four joint names, the aero-frame rotation and the STL normal flip. Cycle-averaged flapsim/fluid/averaged_hover.py Hard-codes identified constants for one robot at one amplitude. Config flapsim/config/*.json, loader.py SingleThrustRobot.json already has an aero_frames section with bodies, axes and signs, but nothing reads it. Actuators, controllers flapsim/actuator/SingleThrustFlapper, flapsim/controller/SingleThrustFlapper Reusable logic (PD position, sinusoidal trajectory, cascaded hover PID) in robot-named packages. Entry point sim_core.py, flapsim.py ROBOT_URDFS dict with one entry; fix=True/False selects the aero model. Robot assets flapsim/robot/SingleThrustFlapper URDF + 7 STL meshes, becomes the first example robot package. Docs tutorial/, log/ Three notebooks, a full aero derivation (zh-CN), two engineering notes. No README, LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING. Tests none The tests/ directory held only bytecode.

Measured on this branch (fixed base, 5e-5 s timestep): 1000 steps in 0.12 s, so one simulated second costs about 2.4 s of wall time. Treat this as the performance floor; the refactor must not make it worse.

Measured again after Phase 7 on the same machine (FLAPSIM_BENCH=1 pytest tests/test_benchmark.py and the setups in examples/):

Setup Steps per second Relative to real time Pre-platform adapter (Phase 0) 8,300 0.42x sim.yaml, engine with the quasi-steady model 6,900 0.35x sim.yaml plus rotational lift, added mass, wake capture 2,800 0.14x hover.yaml, cycle-averaged model 25,100 1.3x

The composable engine costs 17 percent against the hard-wired adapter, inside the 20 percent guard. Each additional per-wing model costs roughly as much as the first; vectorising the models across wings is the next performance step if it matters to users.

docs.title: 3.1 User-facing workflow
docs.text:
import flapsim
from flapsim.aero import QuasiSteadyBladeElement, RotationalLift, AddedMass
from flapsim.actuators import SinusoidalStroke
from flapsim.sensors import IMU
from flapsim.io import Recorder

robot = flapsim.load_robot("my_robot/robot.yaml")  # URDF or MJCF + wing manifest
sim = flapsim.Simulation(robot, timestep=5e-5, base="fixed")

sim.add(QuasiSteadyBladeElement(wings="all") + RotationalLift() + AddedMass())
sim.add(
    SinusoidalStroke(
        joints=["left_stroke", "right_stroke"],
        frequency_hz=35.0,
        amplitude_rad=1.5,
        mirror=True,
    )
)
sim.add(IMU(body="torso", rate_hz=500.0, noise="default"))
sim.add(Recorder(["wings/*/force_world", "imu/*"], every=1e-3))

sim.run(duration=2.0, viewer=False)
table = sim["recorder"].to_numpy()

The same assembly can be written as YAML and run with flapsim run my_robot/sim.yaml --duration 2 --headless.

docs.title: 3.2 Package layout
docs.text:
flapsim/
  core/        Simulation, step pipeline, phases, state views (BodyState, JointState)
  robot/       load URDF/MJCF/MjSpec, RobotManifest schema, patches, parametric builders
  wings/       Wing runtime object: frame, kinematics, planform integrals, CoP
  aero/        AeroModel base, AeroStack, built-in models, force application
  plugins/     Plugin base classes, registry, entry-point discovery, lifecycle
  actuators/   PD position, sinusoidal trajectory, DC motor + crank, servo
  sensors/     IMU, TOF, encoder, force/torque; noise and delay models
  controllers/ PID hover, waypoint tracker, user callback controller
  io/          Recorder (npz, csv, hdf5), telemetry, viewer overlays, video
  config/      schema, YAML/JSON loading, deep merge, validation errors
  cli.py       flapsim run | inspect | convert | sweep
flapsim/assets/robots/   example robot packages shipped with the wheel (single_thrust_flapper/)
examples/      runnable scripts and notebooks (hover, lift sweep, write a plugin)
docs/          mkdocs site: tutorials, concepts, API, derivations (moved from tutorial/, log/)
tests/         unit, regression (golden numbers), plugin-conformance suite

docs.title: 3.3 Core abstractions
docs.text:
Simulation and step pipeline. One Simulation owns MjModel, MjData and an ordered list of plugins. Each step runs the phases pre_control -> control -> actuate -> forces -> mj_step -> post_step -> record. A plugin implements only the phases it needs. This is the existing SimulationEnvironment.step() made explicit and extensible.

RobotManifest. A YAML or JSON file next to the robot model that holds what URDF cannot express. Example for the current robot:

schema: flapsim.robot/1
name: SingleThrustFlapper
model:
  file: urdf/SingleThrustFlapper.urdf          # .urdf, .xml (MJCF) or python:module:function
  root_body: base_link
  spawn: {position: [0.0, 0.0, 0.5]}
  patches:                                     # applied on the MjSpec before compile
    joints:
      left_wing_feathering:  {stiffness: 2.0e-7, armature: 1.0e-10, solref_limit: [4.0e-4, 1.0]}
      right_wing_feathering: {stiffness: 2.0e-7, armature: 1.0e-10, solref_limit: [4.0e-4, 1.0]}
    equalities:
      - {type: joint, joints: [left_wing_feathering, right_wing_feathering], polycoef: [0, 1, 0, 0, 0]}
    exclude_self_collision: true
torso: {body: link2}
wings:
  - name: left
    body: left_wing
    side: left
    frame: {normal: [1, 0, 0], span: [0, 0, -1], chord: [0, 1, 0]}   # aero axes in body frame
    stroke_joint:     {name: left_flapping_joint,  sign: +1}
    feathering_joint: {name: left_wing_feathering, sign: -1}
    planform: {length: 0.07, mean_chord: 0.02, profile: rectangular}
    force_sign: -1                              # mesh normal is opposite to the aero convention
  - name: right
    mirror_of: left                             # frame calibrated at the neutral pose, as today
    body: right_wing
    stroke_joint:     {name: right_wing_flapping,   sign: -1}
    feathering_joint: {name: right_wing_feathering, sign: +1}

Every hard-coded fact in environment.py and mujoco_adapter.py moves into this file. The aero_frames block already in SingleThrustRobot.json is the starting point.

Wing. Built from one manifest entry. Resolves MuJoCo ids once, exposes psi, psi_dot, theta, theta_dot, the world rotation of the aero frame, the body origin and centre of mass, and the planform integrals (r00..r33, z_cp0..z_cp2, z_rd). Integrals come from one of three inputs: the raw numbers (today's Wing.json), a chord polyline c(r) (what tutorial 2 computes), or a mesh outline (stretch goal).

AeroModel plugin. Pure computation, no MuJoCo calls:

class AeroModel(ForcePlugin):
    def compute(self, wing: WingState, body: BodyState, air: Atmosphere) -> WingLoads:
        """Return force and moment in the wing aero frame plus the centre of pressure."""

AeroStack sums the loads of several models for each wing. The core transforms the total to the world frame and applies it at the centre of pressure with mj_applyFT (today the force is applied at the body origin with a torque correction). Atmosphere is itself a plugin: density, wind vector, gust model, ground-effect factor as a function of height.

Component plugins. ActuatorPlugin (writes qfrc_applied, ctrl, or sets kinematic joint state), SensorPlugin (reads state, applies noise and delay, publishes a named signal), ControllerPlugin (reads signals, writes commands), RecorderPlugin (subscribes to signals). Signals are addressed by path such as wings/left/alpha or imu/gyro, so plugins compose without importing each other.

Registry and discovery. flapsim.plugins.register(kind, name, cls) for in-tree classes, plus importlib.metadata entry points in the group flapsim.plugins so a third-party pip install flapsim-myaero is found automatically. Config files refer to plugins by kind/name.

Identification tools. The cycle-averaged hover model is reframed as a tool: flapsim sweep runs a fixed-base frequency and amplitude sweep with any aero stack, fits lift and control-moment coefficients, and writes a CycleAveragedAero parameter file for that robot. No constants in code.

docs.title: 4. Phases
docs.text: Each phase ends with a tagged commit and green CI. Acceptance criteria are written so they can be checked mechanically.

docs.title: Phase 0: clean baseline (done 2026-10-28)
docs.text:
• Branch open-platform cut from master.
  • Removed: flapsim/rl (PPO code and trained models), MUJOCO_LOG.TXT, tracked bytecode, untracked run logs, checkpoints and videos.
  • .gitignore now blocks runs/, artifacts/, checkpoints/, model zips, videos and MuJoCo logs. pyproject.toml lost the dangling rl extra and gained a dev extra.

docs.title: Phase 1: foundations and safety net (done 2026-10-28)
docs.text:
Goal: lock current behaviour in tests before touching any physics code.

  • README.md (English, with a zh-CN section link), LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, CITATION.cff, CHANGELOG.md.
  • Move log/*.md to docs/notes/, tutorial/aero*.md to docs/derivations/, notebooks to examples/notebooks/.
  • tests/: unit tests for normal_force_coefficient, center_of_pressure_fraction, wing_aero, world_wrench; left/right mirror symmetry; a regression test that reproduces the fixed-base lift sweep from docs/notes/aero_force_sign_fix.md (20, 30, 40, 50 Hz) within 1 percent; a headless smoke run for both base modes.
  • GitHub Actions: pytest on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows for Python 3.10 to 3.13; ruff check and ruff format --check.
  • Pin mujoco>=3.3,<4 (MjSpec API) and declare numpy>=1.24.

Acceptance: CI green on all nine matrix cells; the lift-sweep regression test fails if any force sign in the adapter is flipped.

docs.title: Phase 2: robot description and import (done 2026-10-28)
docs.text:
Goal: zero robot-specific names inside flapsim/.

  • RobotManifest schema (dataclasses plus JSON Schema export) and loader for YAML and JSON.
  • flapsim.robot.load() accepting a manifest, a bare URDF or MJCF path, or an MjSpec. Bare files load with no wings and a warning.
  • Manifest patches: joint dynamics, equalities, collision exclusions, free or fixed base, spawn pose. Replaces the inline code in environment.py.
  • Wing runtime object; mirror_of calibration at the neutral pose (the current aero_from_body_right logic).
  • Move flapsim/robot/SingleThrustFlapper to flapsim/assets/robots/single_thrust_flapper/ with robot.yaml, meshes and URDF, packaged as data so pip install flapsim ships the example.
  • flapsim inspect <model>: prints bodies, joints, axes and limits so a user can write a manifest in minutes.
  • flapsim.robot.builders.FlatPlateFlapper(span, chord, ...): a parametric two-wing robot generated in Python, for users without CAD and for tests.
  • Add a xacro preprocessing hook as an optional extra. SDF stays out of scope.

Acceptance: grep -r "left_wing\|link2\|right_wing_flapping" flapsim/ --include=*.py returns nothing outside flapsim/robot/builders.py (which defines its own robot); the Phase 1 regression tests pass unchanged through the manifest path; the builder robot loads, flaps and produces positive mean lift. Result: all three hold. Porting to the manifest first reproduced the Phase 1 lift-sweep values to the last digit, which validated the frame plumbing. The parametric builder robot then exposed a physics defect inherited from the original code: the pitching moment carried a sign(alpha) factor that made it independent of flow direction, so the centre of pressure switched sides of the hinge at each reversal and a force-only flip in the adapter masked the lift sign. The moment was restored to -d_cp c F_N, the flip removed, wing frames redefined by span and chord, and a per-wing mass model added (the URDF's uniform-solid centroid 22 mm behind the hinge gives anti-phase feathering and negative lift; a spar-plate distribution flies). The regression values were re-measured: 0.074, 0.167, 0.297, 0.464 N at 20, 30, 40, 50 Hz, a clean frequency-squared law with hover near 40 Hz for the 30 g robot. Details in docs/derivations/quasi_steady_model.md.

docs.title: Phase 3: plugin system (done 2026-10-28)
docs.text:
Goal: the existing simulation is assembled from plugins and config, not from SimCore.__init__.

  • Plugin base class with lifecycle (bind(sim), reset, phase hooks, signals), Simulation with ordered phases.
  • Registry, entry-point discovery, kind/name resolution from config.
  • Port PositionController, TrajectoryController, PlateController, ThrustController, HoveringController, MuJoCoAeroAdapter and AveragedHoverAero to plugins. Keep thin compatibility shims in sim_core.py and flapsim.py for one release, with deprecation warnings.
  • flapsim run sim.yaml builds everything from a file.
  • Plugin-conformance test suite that third-party authors can run against their own plugin (pytest --pyargs flapsim.testing.conformance).

Acceptance: python flapsim.py --robot SingleThrustFlapper --headless --duration 1 still works and produces the same lift-sweep numbers; a dummy plugin installed from a separate directory is discovered by entry point and runs. Result: both hold. SimCore now builds the shipped sim.yaml / hover.yaml through Simulation.from_config; the regression values are unchanged. Entry-point discovery is covered by a test with a fake distribution entry point. The old flapsim.environment, flapsim.actuator and flapsim.controller packages were removed rather than shimmed: the branch is pre-release and SimCore plus flapsim.fluid remain as the compatibility surface.

docs.title: Phase 4: aerodynamics library (done 2026-10-28)
docs.text:
Goal: a documented, tested set of aero plugins that work for any number of wings and any frame.

  • QuasiSteadyBladeElement: generalise aero.py to N wings, arbitrary frame and stroke-plane definitions from the manifest, forces applied at the CoP.
  • CycleAveragedAero: parameter file produced by flapsim sweep; no built-in constants; mass handling declared in the manifest instead of overriding to 30 g.
  • New plugins, each with a unit test against an analytic or published case: RotationalLift (Sane and Dickinson rotational circulation), AddedMass, WakeCapture (empirical), BodyDrag (per-body drag coefficients), GroundEffect, Atmosphere with steady wind and gust models.
  • WingPlanform utilities: integrals from a chord polyline, from a mesh outline, and the reverse (export the planform used).
  • Diagnostics as signals: alpha, C_N, F_N, CoP, per-model contributions, so users can plot which effect produced which force.
  • Performance guard: benchmark test records steps per second; fail if slower than the Phase 0 floor by more than 20 percent. Optional numba path if needed.

Acceptance: FlapX parity test still passes for the two-wing robot; a four-wing builder robot runs with the same plugin; each effect toggles independently. Result: the lift regression holds through the engine (single-model stack equals the legacy adapter to machine precision); models are additive and toggle independently; flapsim sweep identifies the cycle-averaged parameters and aero/cycle_averaged loads them. The four-wing builder is deferred to the examples in Phase 7. See docs/aero_models.md.

docs.title: Phase 5: component plugins (done 2026-10-28)
docs.text:
• Actuators: PD position, sinusoidal trajectory, DCMotorCrank (motor model plus crank or gear kinematics, from dc_motor.json), servo with rate limit.
  • Sensors: IMU, TOF range, joint encoder, body force and torque; noise, bias and delay models that reproduce rl_imu_hover/sensors.py from the ppo branch.
  • Controllers: HoverPID (generalised from HoveringController), waypoint tracker, CallbackController for user Python functions.
  • IO: Recorder (npz, csv, hdf5), viewer overlays drawing force arrows and CoP markers per wing, offscreen video rendering.

Acceptance: an examples/hover_pid.py holds altitude with the example robot; examples/sensors.py logs IMU and TOF to a file and plots them. Result: both scripts run in the test suite. The DC motor model loads itself from the aero plugin's wing torques, so stroke frequency responds to voltage and aerodynamic load; the load cell reads MuJoCo's constraint wrench on the root body. Video export renders offscreen (OSMesa/EGL) to GIF, PNG frames or MP4 when imageio is installed.

docs.title: Phase 6: learning and optimisation integration (done 2026-10-28)
docs.text:
• flapsim[rl]: a generic Gymnasium wrapper over Simulation with observation and action spaces assembled from named signals and commands.
  • Recreate the ppo branch's IMU plus TOF hover task as examples/rl/ using only public plugin APIs. The old code stays in git history.
  • flapsim sweep and a ParameterStudy helper for design optimisation (wing length, frequency, amplitude) with multiprocessing.

Acceptance: the example PPO task trains for a smoke run in CI without touching flapsim/core. Result: flapsim.envs.SimulationEnv (Gymnasium) with signal observations and command actions, hover_reward/hover_terminated, flapsim.study for parallel parameter studies; examples/rl/ rebuilds the IMU + TOF hover task and trains PPO; a dedicated CI job installs the rl extra and runs the smoke training.

docs.title: Phase 7: documentation, examples, release (done 2026-10-28)
docs.text:
• MkDocs Material site with mkdocstrings: Getting started, Import your robot, Define wings, Choose aerodynamics, Write a plugin, Run RL, Derivations (translated from tutorial/aero.md), API reference.
  • Example gallery with rendered videos.
  • v0.2.0 on PyPI (flapsim is unclaimed as of 2026-10-28), GitHub release notes, Zenodo DOI, issue and PR templates.
  • Optional: JOSS paper draft once two external users have imported a robot.

Result: MkDocs Material site (mkdocs.yml, docs/) with getting started, manifest tutorial, aero models, components, plugin guide, CLI, learning, gallery (rendered GIFs), derivations (English conventions page plus translations of the Chinese originals), engineering notes and an mkdocstrings API reference; docs.yml builds it on every push and deploys to GitHub Pages from master; release.yml builds and publishes on v* tags. Version 0.2.0 set in pyproject.toml, CITATION.cff and the package. The JOSS paper is left for later.

docs.title: 5. Validation strategy
docs.text:
• Golden numbers. Fixed-base lift sweep at 1.5 rad amplitude: 20, 30, 40, 50 Hz mean lift, plus the FlapX phase-resolved comparison. Any refactor must reproduce them.
  • Symmetry. Mirrored wings produce mirrored forces at every phase.
  • Analytic limits. Flat plate in steady flow matches C_N(alpha); pure feathering rotation produces opposing damping moment; zero velocity produces zero force.
  • Conservation checks. Fixed-base reaction force equals the sum of wing forces plus gravity, read back from MuJoCo.
  • Cross-robot. The same aero plugin passes on the CAD robot and on the parametric builder robot.
  • Plugin conformance. Third-party plugins run the shared conformance suite.

docs.title: 6. Decisions needed from the maintainer
docs.text:
1. License. Recommended: Apache-2.0 (patent grant, common in robotics) or MIT. Must be compatible with FlapX, whose quasi-steady model and empirical C_N and d_cp fits this code reproduces. Verify the FlapX license and add attribution in README.md and aero.py before the first public release.
  2. Documentation language. Proposed: English primary, zh-CN translations of tutorials and derivations kept in docs/zh/.
  3. Package and repository names. Keep flapsim for both.
  4. RL code. Return as examples/rl/ inside this repo (proposed) or as a separate flapsim-rl repository.
  5. Support matrix. Proposed: Linux, macOS, Windows; Python 3.10 to 3.13; MuJoCo 3.3 and newer.

docs.title: 7. Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Coordinate and sign conventions regress while generalising (the fixes in docs/notes/aero_force_sign_fix.md were hard won). Phase 1 regression tests before any refactor; manifest fields sign and force_sign make conventions explicit and testable. Per-step Python aero becomes the bottleneck with more wings and more models. Benchmark gate in CI; vectorise across wings with NumPy; optional numba. MjSpec API changes between MuJoCo releases. Pin mujoco>=3.3,<4; CI runs the newest and the oldest supported version. Scope creep in aerodynamic models. Ship quasi-steady and cycle-averaged first; everything else is a plugin with its own test. Users cannot write a manifest for their URDF. flapsim inspect, a documented worked example, and a validator with precise error messages.

docs.title: 8. Decisions taken
docs.text:
• 2026-10-28: Apache-2.0 license; English documentation with the Chinese originals kept under docs/zh/; execute all phases in order.
  • Example robots live inside the package (flapsim/assets/robots/) so that a plain pip install flapsim ships them; the parametric builder robots live in flapsim.robot.builders.

docs.title: 9. Release checklist for 0.2.0 (maintainer actions)
docs.text:
1. Merge open-platform into master (the CI, docs and release workflows watch master).
  2. Enable GitHub Pages for the repository (source: the gh-pages branch that mkdocs gh-deploy creates on the first push to master).
  3. On pypi.org, register a trusted publisher for MingshanHe/FlapSim, workflow release.yml, environment pypi, and create the pypi environment in the repository settings. The project name flapsim was unclaimed on 2026-10-28.
  4. Tag and push: git tag v0.2.0 && git push origin v0.2.0. The workflow builds the wheel and sdist, publishes to PyPI and creates the GitHub release with generated notes.
  5. Optional: link the repository to Zenodo before tagging so the release receives a DOI, then add the DOI badge and doi field to CITATION.cff.
  6. Announce; the first external robot imports will show where the manifest tutorial needs more detail.

docs.title: Import your robot
docs.text: FlapSim loads URDF and MJCF through MuJoCo's MjSpec. What those formats cannot say about a flapping robot goes into a manifest, robot.yaml, next to the model file.

docs.title: 1. Inspect the model
docs.text:
flapsim inspect my_robot.urdf

prints every body with its parent and mass, every joint with its type, axis and range, and the sites. Note the wing bodies, the stroke joints and the passive feathering joints.

docs.title: 2. Write the manifest
docs.text:
schema: flapsim.robot/1
name: MyFlapper
aliases: [my_flapper]

model:
  file: urdf/my_robot.urdf        # relative to this file; .xml for MJCF
  root_body: base_link            # a direct child of the world body
  base: {type: fixed, position: [0.0, 0.0, 0.5]}
  timestep: 5.0e-5
  integrator: implicitfast
  patches:                        # what URDF cannot express
    joints:
      left_feathering:  {stiffness: 2.0e-7, armature: 1.0e-10,
                         solref_limit: [4.0e-4, 1.0]}
      right_feathering: {stiffness: 2.0e-7, armature: 1.0e-10,
                         solref_limit: [4.0e-4, 1.0]}
    equalities:
      - {type: joint, targets: [left_feathering, right_feathering], polycoef: [0, 1]}
    bodies:
      base_link: {when: free, mass: 0.03, com: [0, 0, 0],
                  fullinertia: [5.0e-5, 5.0e-5, 2.0e-5, 0, 0, 0]}
    exclude_self_collision: true

torso: {body: torso}              # body whose velocity the aero models use
air_density: 1.225

wings:
  - name: left
    body: left_wing
    side: left
    frame:
      span: [0.0, 0.0, -1.0]      # root -> tip, along the feathering axis (body frame)
      chord: [0.0, -1.0, 0.0]     # leading edge (hinge) -> trailing edge
    stroke_joint: {name: left_stroke, sign: 1}
    feathering_joint: {name: left_feathering, sign: 1}
    planform: {profile: rectangular, length: 0.07, mean_chord: 0.02}
    mass_model: {type: spar_plate, mass: 6.26e-5, spar_fraction: 0.8}
    shoulder_offset: 0.014
  - name: right
    body: right_wing
    side: right
    mirror_of: left               # shares the left frame at the neutral pose
    stroke_joint: {name: right_stroke, sign: -1}
    feathering_joint: {name: right_feathering, sign: 1}
    planform: {profile: rectangular, length: 0.07, mean_chord: 0.02}
    mass_model: {type: spar_plate, mass: 6.26e-5, spar_fraction: 0.8}
    shoulder_offset: 0.014

docs.title: Wing frame
docs.text: span points from the wing root to the tip along the feathering axis; chord points from the leading edge (the hinge line) towards the trailing edge. Both are unit-free vectors in the wing body's frame. FlapSim derives the surface normal, so the side of the hinge on which the plate lies is never ambiguous. A site whose +X is the chord and +Y the span works too. A mirrored wing can simply say mirror_of: <other wing>.

docs.title: Joint signs
docs.text:
Positive stroke angle is a right-handed rotation about the stroke axis (side * Z of the aero frame), positive feathering angle a right-handed rotation about +Y for both wings. sign converts the MuJoCo joint coordinate. If you get it wrong the loader warns:

wing 'left': positive stroke_joint rate is not a right-handed rotation about
side * Z (the stroke axis); flip the joint's 'sign'.

It also warns when the wing's centre of mass lies on the wrong side of the hinge for the chosen chord.

docs.title: Planform
docs.text:
• rectangular or elliptic with length and mean_chord;
  • polyline: chord_polyline: [[r, c], ...] in metres from root to tip;
  • integrals: the eight blade-element integrals directly;
  • pitch_axis_fraction (hinge inside the chord) or leading_edge_offset (root spar between hinge and leading edge).

flapsim.wings.from_polygon and from_mesh compute the integrals from an outline or an STL file.

docs.title: Mass model
docs.text: CAD exports often place a wing's centroid far behind the hinge. For a membrane wing that is unphysical, and it inverts the passive feathering phase (negative lift). Declare mass_model in wing coordinates (normal, span, chord), so mirrored wings share the same numbers: spar_plate (a leading-edge spar carrying spar_fraction of the mass plus a membrane plate), thin_plate, or explicit (com, diaginertia).

docs.title: 3. Load and check
docs.text:
from flapsim.robot import load

robot = load("path/to/robot.yaml")  # or base="free"
print(robot.wings, robot.geometry_warnings())

flapsim inspect path/to/robot.yaml          # lists the resolved wings too

docs.title: 4. Give it a setup file
docs.text: Copy sim.yaml from the example robot, change the joint names, and run flapsim run path/to/sim.yaml. Robots without CAD can start from flapsim.robot.flat_plate_flapper(), which builds a two-wing flat-plate robot and its manifest in Python.

docs.title: flapsim.aero.base
docs.text:
Composable aerodynamics: flow state, per-wing kinematics, model loads.

An :class:AeroModel turns one wing's kinematics into :class:WingLoads (a force at a point plus a pure moment, all in the wing aero frame). An :class:AeroEngine evaluates the shared kinematics once per wing, sums the loads of every model, applies :class:AeroModifier factors (for example ground effect) and writes the resulting wrench to MuJoCo. Plugins wrap the engine; see :mod:flapsim.aero.stack.

docs.title: FlowState dataclass
docs.text: Torso velocity relative to the air and the air properties, per step.

docs.title: WingLoads dataclass
docs.text:
Loads of one model on one wing, in the wing aero frame.

force acts at point (relative to the wing body origin); moment is a pure couple. diagnostics are scalars published as wings/<wing>/<model>/<key>.

docs.title: AeroModel
docs.text: Base class of additive per-wing aerodynamic models.

docs.title: bind(robot)
docs.text:
Called once when an engine is built for robot (optional hook).

Models that need to modify the MuJoCo model, for example to add an implicit added inertia to a joint, do it here.

docs.title: reset()
docs.text: Forget any history (called when the simulation resets).

docs.title: AeroModifier
docs.text: Multiplies the summed loads of a wing by a factor (ground effect ...).

docs.title: AeroEngine
docs.text: Evaluate a stack of models on every wing of a robot and apply them.

docs.title: apply(flow=None)
docs.text: Compute all loads for the current state and write them to MuJoCo.

docs.title: flapsim.aero.models.quasi_steady
docs.text: Translational quasi-steady normal force (Whitney & Wood 2010 / FlapX).

docs.title: QuasiSteadyModel
docs.text:
Bases: AeroModel

Normal force F_N at the centre of pressure plus rotational damping.

Diagnostics: alpha, C_N, d_cp, M_aero, M_rd, chord_CoP, span_CoP, F_N_raw. options overrides the engine's :class:~flapsim.config.AeroOptions for this model only.

docs.title: flapsim.aero.models.rotational_lift
docs.text: Rotational circulation force (Sane & Dickinson 2002).

docs.title: RotationalLift
docs.text:
Bases: AeroModel

F_rot = C_rot rho theta_dot * integral c(r)^2 |U(r)| dr along the normal.

C_rot = pi (0.75 - x0) by default, with x0 the hinge position as a fraction of the chord (Sane & Dickinson 2002, eq. 4). Positive when the wing pitches up relative to the oncoming flow. The force acts at the point_fraction of the chord behind the leading edge (default half chord) at the spanwise centre of pressure. Diagnostics: C_rot, circulation_integral.

docs.title: flapsim.aero.models.added_mass
docs.text: Added-mass (non-circulatory) loads of a thin flat-plate wing.

docs.title: AddedMass
docs.text:
Bases: AeroModel

Reaction of the accelerated fluid on a thin flat-plate wing.

Per unit span the added mass of a flat plate moving normal to itself is m_a = rho pi c^2 / 4. The model splits its effect in two:

  • Explicit force from the prescribed accelerations: the normal flow at section r is U_n(r) = U_i1 r + U_i0 (stroke and body motion); its time derivative over one step gives F = integral m_a dU_n/dt dr along the normal, applied at the mid-chord of the c^2-weighted span centroid.
  • Implicit inertia for the passive feathering: the added rotational inertia about the hinge (:func:feathering_added_inertia) is added to the feathering joint's armature when the model is bound. Applying it as an explicit force from a finite-difference feathering acceleration is unstable for light wings, because the added inertia then lags the motion by one step; MuJoCo integrates armature implicitly.

include_feathering_inertia=False skips the armature change. The armature uses the manifest's air density at bind time. Diagnostics: dU_i1, dU_i0, added_inertia.

docs.title: feathering_added_inertia(params, rho, c4=1.0)
docs.text:
Added rotational inertia of a flat plate about its feathering hinge.

Per unit span the plate carries m_a = rho pi c^2 / 4 at its mid-chord, a distance d_mid from the hinge, plus the added inertia rho pi c^4 / 128 about the mid-chord (Sedov). Integrated over the span with the planform integrals (c^2 -> z_cp0, c^4 -> c4).

docs.title: flapsim.aero.models.wake_capture
docs.text: Empirical wake-capture force after stroke reversal (Dickinson et al. 1999).

docs.title: WakeCapture
docs.text:
Bases: AeroModel

Transient normal force when the wing meets the wake it shed before reversal.

Empirical: when the relative flow U_i at the span centre of pressure changes sign, the velocity magnitude just before reversal U_rev is stored and a force C_wc 1/2 rho S U_rev^2 exp(-(t - t_rev) / tau) is applied along the new flow direction, with tau = tau_chords c / U_rev. C_wc and tau_chords are tuning constants (defaults 1.0 and 0.5); there is no first-principles value. Diagnostics: U_rev, elapsed.

docs.title: flapsim.aero.models.ground_effect
docs.text: Ground-effect lift augmentation as a multiplicative factor.

docs.title: GroundEffect
docs.text:
Bases: AeroModifier

Scale a wing's loads by a factor that grows near the ground.

exponential: 1 + gain * exp(-h / (length_scale * R)) with h the height of the wing's origin above ground_height. cheeseman_bennett: the rotor-in-ground-effect formula 1 / (1 - (R / (4 h))^2), capped at max_factor. Both are empirical and tuned by the user.

docs.title: flapsim.aero.stack
docs.text: Aero plugins built on :class:~flapsim.aero.base.AeroEngine.

docs.title: AeroStack
docs.text:
Bases: AeroPlugin

Sum several additive aero models on every wing, with modifiers.

models lists model names or {type: name, ...} mappings (see flapsim.aero.base.available_models()), modifiers likewise. Reads atmosphere/rho and atmosphere/wind_world when an atmosphere plugin publishes them. Publishes aero/F_world, aero/lift_total, aero/rho and per wing wings/<name>/<key> totals plus wings/<name>/<model>/<key> contributions. imposed_body_velocity and imposed_body_rates replace the torso velocity seen by the models (identification and testing only).

docs.title: QuasiSteadyAero
docs.text:
Bases: AeroStack

Per-step quasi-steady blade-element forces (the single-model stack).

Publishes aero/F_world, aero/lift_total and, for every wing, wings/<name>/F_N, alpha, F_world, torque_world, cop_world and the quasi_steady/ contributions (C_N, M_aero, M_rd, chord_CoP, span_CoP). options are :class:~flapsim.config.AeroOptions fields.

docs.title: flapsim.aero.atmosphere
docs.text: Air density, steady wind, gusts and turbulence.

docs.title: Atmosphere
docs.text:
Bases: AtmospherePlugin

Publish atmosphere/rho and atmosphere/wind_world every step.

rho defaults to the ISA density at altitude_m. wind is a steady world-frame vector; gust adds one of one_minus_cos (amplitude, start, duration, direction), sine (amplitude, frequency_hz, direction, phase) or step (amplitude, start, direction); turbulence adds an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process per axis (sigma m/s, tau s, seed). Add this plugin before the aero plugins that should see the wind.

docs.title: isa_density(altitude_m)
docs.text: International Standard Atmosphere density in the troposphere [kg/m^3].

docs.title: flapsim.aero.body_drag
docs.text: Quadratic drag on bodies (fuselage, legs, tail).

docs.title: BodyDrag
docs.text:
Bases: ForcePlugin

F = -1/2 rho C_d A |v| v per body axis, relative to the wind.

bodies maps body names to {cd, area} where each may be a scalar (isotropic) or a 3-vector in the body frame. Density comes from atmosphere/rho when published, else rho or the manifest. Forces are added to xfrc_applied at the body centre of mass, so place this plugin after any plugin that overwrites a body's wrench. Publishes <id>/<body>/F_world.

docs.title: flapsim.aero.cycle_averaged
docs.text:
Cycle-averaged lift and control moments for floating-base hover studies.

The robot is treated as one rigid body. Lift k f^2 acts along the body thrust axis, tilted by the gimbal angles; gimbal angles also produce control moments, scaled by (f / f_ref)^2; linear and angular damping oppose the body velocity. All coefficients can be identified from the per-step model with :func:flapsim.aero.identify.identify_cycle_averaged (flapsim sweep) and loaded from the resulting parameter file.

docs.title: CycleAveragedAero
docs.text: Bases: AeroPlugin

docs.title: hover_frequency_hz property
docs.text: Frequency at which the cycle-averaged lift balances the robot weight.

docs.title: flapsim.aero.identify
docs.text:
Identify cycle-averaged parameters from the per-step model.

The fixed-base robot is a virtual wind tunnel: sweep the stroke frequency to fit the lift coefficient, deflect each gimbal joint to measure how the mean force direction and the mean moment change per radian, and impose body velocities and rates on the aero stack to measure damping. The result is a flapsim.cycle_averaged/1 parameter file for :class:~flapsim.aero.cycle_averaged.CycleAveragedAero.

docs.title: lift_sweep(make_sim, frequencies, *, amplitude_rad=None, settle=0.2, cycles=10.0, stroke_id='stroke', aero_id='aero')
docs.text: Mean world force per frequency and the least-squares lift = k f^2 fit.

docs.title: gimbal_sensitivity(make_sim, *, frequency_hz, joints=None, angle_rad=0.1, settle=0.2, cycles=10.0, stroke_id='stroke', gimbal_id='gimbal', aero_id='aero')
docs.text:
Per gimbal joint: d(mean force)/d(angle) and d(mean torque)/d(angle).

Central differences at +/- angle_rad; forces and torques are expressed in the root body frame.

docs.title: damping_sensitivity(make_sim, *, frequency_hz, speed=0.5, rate=1.0, settle=0.2, cycles=10.0, stroke_id='stroke', aero_id='aero')
docs.text:
Linear and angular damping from imposed body velocities and rates.

Returns linear (-dF_i/dv_i) and angular (-dT_i/dw_i) in the root body frame, using central differences on the aero stack's imposed body velocity and rates.

docs.title: identify_cycle_averaged(make_sim, *, frequencies=(20.0, 30.0, 40.0, 50.0), reference_frequency_hz=None, amplitude_rad=None, gimbal_angle_rad=0.1, include_damping=True, settle=0.2, cycles=10.0, stroke_id='stroke', gimbal_id='gimbal', aero_id='aero')
docs.text: Run all sweeps and assemble a flapsim.cycle_averaged/1 parameter set.

docs.title: flapsim.fluid.aero
docs.text:
Quasi-steady blade-element aerodynamics for one flapping wing.

Pure functions, no MuJoCo state. Inputs and outputs use SI units.

docs.title: Wing aero frame
docs.text:
+X is the surface normal, +Y the feathering (span) axis and +Z = X x Y. The feathering axis runs along the leading edge and the chord extends from it along -Z, so the centre of pressure always lies at [0, side * span_CoP, -chord_CoP] with chord_CoP >= 0. Positive psi is a right-handed stroke rotation about side * Z and positive theta a right-handed feathering rotation about +Y; side is +1 for a left wing and -1 for its mirror image, which shares the same frame orientation at the neutral pose. U_i is the relative flow speed along +X at the span centre of pressure, so F_N carries the sign of the flow and M_aero = -d_cp * c * F_N always turns the trailing edge downstream, which is what drives passive feathering.

wrench follows MuJoCo's world-frame order [Fx, Fy, Fz, Tx, Ty, Tz] about the wing centre of mass. The formulation follows Whitney & Wood (2010) as used by the FlapX simulator.

docs.title: wing_kinematics(params, side, psi, psi_dot, theta, theta_dot, linear_velocity_body, angular_velocity_body, options=None)
docs.text:
Relative-flow coefficients and angle of attack of one wing.

The flow along +X (U_i) and along +Z (U_o) is affine in the span coordinate: U = U1 * r + U0. The angle of attack is evaluated at the spanwise centre of pressure r_cp = R r33 / r22.

docs.title: wing_loads_from_kinematics(params, kin, options=None)
docs.text: Normal force, pitching moment and damping from :func:wing_kinematics.

docs.title: wing_aero(params, side, psi, psi_dot, theta, theta_dot, linear_velocity_body, angular_velocity_body, options=None)
docs.text: Calculate one wing's local aerodynamic force, moments and CoP.

docs.title: world_wrench(wing, side, aero, read_only=False)
docs.text: Convert one wing's local aero result into a world-frame wrench.

docs.title: normal_force_coefficient(alpha)
docs.text: FlapX C_N(alpha) empirical fit.

docs.title: center_of_pressure_fraction(alpha)
docs.text: FlapX chordwise d_cp(alpha) empirical fit.

docs.title: flapsim.actuators.sinusoidal_stroke
docs.text: Kinematic sinusoidal stroke: q = direction * A sin(2 pi f t + phase).

docs.title: SinusoidalStroke
docs.text:
Bases: ActuatorPlugin

Impose a sinusoidal angle on one or more stroke joints.

kinematic mode writes position and velocity (so aerodynamic models see the stroke rate); position_only writes the position with zero velocity, which the cycle-averaged floating model uses to avoid injecting energy. Commands cmd/<id>/frequency_hz and cmd/<id>/amplitude_rad override the configured values; the current values are published as <id>/frequency_hz, <id>/amplitude_rad and <id>/phase.

docs.title: flapsim.actuators.pd_position
docs.text: PD position actuator with torque limits, or a kinematic position hold.

docs.title: PDPosition
docs.text:
Bases: ActuatorPlugin

Hold joints at targets with a gravity-compensated PD law.

joints maps joint names to {kp, kd, max_torque, target, role}. role is a free label (for example pitch or roll) that lets controllers address joints by function. Targets come from cmd/<id>/<joint> signals when present and are clipped to the joint range; the active targets are published as <id>/<joint>. In kinematic mode the joint is set to the target after each step.

docs.title: flapsim.actuators.servo
docs.text: Position servo: PD hold with a rate-limited, first-order lagged target.

docs.title: Servo
docs.text:
Bases: PDPosition

A :class:PDPosition whose targets move towards the commanded values at most rate_limit_rad_s fast through a first-order lag of time_constant_s (0 for none), like a hobby servo. Publishes <id>/<joint> (current target) and <id>/<joint>/desired.

docs.title: set_target(joint_name, value, *, clip=False)
docs.text: Jump the servo (and its desired value) to value immediately.

docs.title: flapsim.actuators.dc_motor_crank
docs.text: Brushed DC motor driving the stroke through a gearbox and crank.

docs.title: DCMotorCrank
docs.text:
Bases: ActuatorPlugin

Voltage-driven DC motor, gearbox and crank imposing q = d A sin(theta_c).

Electrical: i = (V - k_e w) / R, tau_m = k_t i. Mechanical, on the motor shaft: J dw/dt = tau_m - b w - c sign(w) + tau_aero / N where tau_aero is the aerodynamic torque about the stroke joints projected onto the crank (load: aero, from the aero plugin's wing signals) and N the gear ratio. The crank angle theta_c advances at w / N and every stroke joint follows direction * A sin(theta_c + phase). Commands: cmd/<id>/voltage_v. Publishes speed_rad_s, frequency_hz, current_a, voltage_v, torque_motor, torque_load, power_w, crank_angle.

docs.title: no_load_speed(voltage_v=None)
docs.text: Motor speed where the back-EMF balances the voltage (no friction).

docs.title: flapsim.sensors.noise
docs.text: Measurement conditioning shared by the sensor plugins.

docs.title: Conditioner
docs.text:
Sample-and-hold, first-order low-pass, pure delay, noise, bias, quantization.

update(true_value, time) returns the current reading. A new sample is taken whenever time reaches the next sampling instant (rate_hz; every call when None). The sample passes a low-pass with time constant tau (seconds, 0 disables), enters a delay line of round(delay_s * rate) samples, then receives Gaussian noise of standard deviation noise_std, a bias drawn uniformly from [-bias_range, bias_range] at every :meth:reset, and is quantised to multiples of resolution (0 disables). All parameters may be scalars or arrays matching size.

docs.title: flapsim.sensors.imu
docs.text: Inertial measurement unit: attitude estimate, gyro and accelerometer.

docs.title: IMU
docs.text:
Bases: SensorPlugin

Attitude (AHRS-like low-pass of the true angles), body rates and specific force at rate_hz.

Defaults reproduce the IMU model used for the IMU-only hover policies: attitude low-pass 20 ms with 0.02 degree noise, gyro noise 0.002 rad/s, accelerometer noise 0.02 m/s^2 with a per-episode bias of up to 0.01 m/s^2. The accelerometer measures R^T (a - g), so a hovering or resting body reads [0, 0, +9.81]. Publishes <id>/euler, <id>/gyro, <id>/accel and <id>/quat (true attitude, for reference).

docs.title: rotation_to_rpy(rotation)
docs.text: Body-to-world rotation matrix to roll, pitch, yaw (Z-Y-X, radians).

docs.title: flapsim.sensors.rangefinder
docs.text: Downward (or any-direction) range finder such as a time-of-flight sensor.

docs.title: RangeFinder
docs.text:
Bases: SensorPlugin

Slant range along a body-fixed direction, delayed and noisy.

plane intersects the ray with the ground plane z = ground_height (the slant range is height / cos(tilt) with cos clamped at min_cos); ray casts a MuJoCo ray against all geoms. Defaults reproduce the hover-policy TOF: 20 ms delay, 5 mm noise, 4 m range, and a range rate from differenced readings through a 50 ms low-pass. Publishes <id>/range and <id>/range_rate.

docs.title: flapsim.sensors.encoder
docs.text: Joint position and velocity measurements.

docs.title: JointEncoder
docs.text:
Bases: SensorPlugin

Quantised, noisy joint positions and velocities at rate_hz.

counts_per_rev sets the position resolution of hinge joints (None for continuous). Publishes <id>/<joint>/position and <id>/<joint>/velocity.

docs.title: flapsim.sensors.wrench
docs.text: Load cell: the interaction wrench between a body and its parent.

docs.title: BodyWrench
docs.text:
Bases: SensorPlugin

Force and torque transmitted from a body's parent (MuJoCo cfrc_int).

For the root body of a fixed-base robot this is the reaction of the mounting, that is the force a load cell under the robot would read (its weight minus the lift). Values are in the world frame about the body's centre of mass, averaged over average_s seconds when given. Publishes <id>/force and <id>/torque.

docs.title: flapsim.controllers.hover_pid
docs.text: Cascaded altitude and attitude PID for hovering with a floating base.

docs.title: HoverPID
docs.text:
Bases: ControllerPlugin

Hold a position (or cycle through waypoints) with a flapping-frequency altitude loop and a gimbal attitude loop.

State is averaged over one stroke period and the loops update once per period. Commands are published for a stroke actuator (cmd/<stroke>/frequency_hz) and a gimbal actuator (cmd/<gimbal>/<pitch_joint>, cmd/<gimbal>/<roll_joint>).

docs.title: flapsim.controllers.schedule
docs.text: Time-scheduled set points for any plugin's commands.

docs.title: SetpointSchedule
docs.text:
Bases: ControllerPlugin

Publish cmd/<target>/<name> from [[time, value], ...] tables.

With interpolate the value is linearly interpolated between the table times, otherwise it holds the latest entry (step changes). Before the first time nothing is published, so the plugin's own default applies. Useful for frequency ramps, gimbal step inputs and scripted manoeuvres.

docs.title: flapsim.controllers.callback
docs.text: Run a user Python function as a controller.

docs.title: CallbackController
docs.text:
Bases: ControllerPlugin

Call callback(sim, controller) -> {command: value} at rate_hz.

Returned keys are published as commands: "stroke/frequency_hz" becomes cmd/stroke/frequency_hz (keys already starting with cmd/ are used as is). None or an empty mapping publishes nothing. The controller keeps a state dictionary for the callback's own use.

docs.title: flapsim.io.recorder
docs.text: Sample signals into memory and export them.

docs.title: MemoryRecorder
docs.text:
Bases: RecorderPlugin

Record matching signals every every seconds (default: every step).

signals is a list of shell-style patterns ("aero/F_world", "wings/*/alpha"). Use :meth:get for one signal as an array of shape (samples, ...), :meth:to_dict, :meth:to_npz or :meth:to_csv.

docs.title: to_hdf5(path)
docs.text: Write one dataset per signal (needs h5py).

docs.title: to_csv(path)
docs.text: Write one row per sample; vector signals expand to name[i] columns.

docs.title: flapsim.io.overlays
docs.text: Viewer and renderer overlays: force arrows and centre-of-pressure markers.

docs.title: ForceArrows
docs.text:
Draw each wing's aerodynamic force as an arrow from its centre of pressure.

Use as sim.run(viewer=True, on_frame=ForceArrows()) or pass it to the video recorder. scale is metres of arrow per newton. The callable accepts a viewer handle (uses user_scn) or an MjvScene.
